newsitem.title: USA: Bear Stearns' Angell sees strong US economy in '97.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns' Angell sees strong US economy in '97.

text.p: Wayne Angell, chief economist, Bear Stearns Co Inc, and a former U.S. Federal Reserve governor, said Friday the U.S. economy should remain strong in 1997, continuing the theme seen in 1996.
"We ended 1996 on something of high note...the economy is alive and well," Angell told a business group here, adding that he anticipated economic growth in 1997 "on the high side of 2.5" percent.
Angell also predicted a Federal funds rate at 5.5 percent by year's end. The current perceived target for the Fed funds rate is 5.25 percent.

But Angell called his Fed funds rate forecast "a crazy prediction...because if the Fed hasn't been raising rates and it raises rates once, it'll probably raise them twice. So maybe we've got a 40-percent chance they won't raise them at all and a 35-percent chance they'll raise them twice. And here I am, clearly in the middle."
Angell also said that average hourly earnings are an area for the Fed to watch.
"Average hourly earnings are continuing to move up, and that's what the Fed worries about," he said.
Angell forecast December-over-December yearly gains in average hourly earnings of 3.9 percent in 1997, 4.2 percent in 1998, and 4.5 percent in 1999. Average hourly earnings in 1996 rose 3.6 percent.
He also said he hopes the Fed will keep an eye on gold, noting that because of the recent fall in the price of gold, "we have altered down our inflation numbers for 1997."
Angell said he had lowered his overall consumer price index forecast for 1997 to 3.0 percent, down from the 3.4 percent his firm had forecast six months ago.
He also said he expected core CPI inflation to rise toward 3.0 percent this year. Core CPI rose 2.6 percent in 1996. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
